challenge.better_approach: Considered running every proof that names a changed id. That is the whole suite in the worst case, and running proofs from a migrate breaks 'judges nothing, moves the plan'. Naming them is cheap (2 s, AST) and keeps the run with the tester.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That readers use a lookup call named *ticket* or a glob. Readers that open a path built elsewhere are missed; the docstring calls a hit 'a lead, not a verdict'.
challenge.prior_art: 149b's own proof's imports_of_the_inspector uses the same AST plus module-bound-name rule. Grepped tickets/ and questions/ for plan_readers: nothing.
challenge.real_collision: None. aa3e9a70db47 is PROVED and its nine teeth are unchanged; this adds a field and a tooth under a new ticket.

answers.falsifier: Done when a changed ticket's report names a tracked reader beside the commons and names no fixture-only, untracked or unchanged case; over the 551ad436 set it names 149b's proof. Wrong intent if readers read plans by a pattern the AST rule misses. The live measure names the one known breaker, but recall beyond it is unmeasured.
answers.how: plan_migration gains plan_readers(repo, ids): an AST read of every tracked proofs/*.py in the cairn repo beside the commons, counting a proof that hands an id to a ticket lookup (a call named *ticket*, or a glob) and reads a plan field by subscript or .get. migrate adds plan_readers to each report; main prints them to stderr as the proofs to run. Tooth 10 in the migrate's own proof lays a git-indexed scratch cairn beside the scratch commons.
answers.traces_to: Law 3: the migrate's '0 reds' was an unmeasured claim about the plan's readers. Law 8: a hollow green (0 reds over a broken reader) is worse than a red.
answers.what: A plan migrate's report names, for each ticket it changes, the tracked proofs that look that ticket up and read a plan field of it, so a migrate cannot report clean while a reader of the plan it rewrote goes red.

bullets.text: the 551ad436 migrate's 0 reds hid one red reader; the report now names readers
